signals_considered.verdict: THE DAY'S BEST FRESH COMMODITY SIGNAL, and not publishable as a new idea. A new Ministry of Steel monthly report landed (the committed series now runs to SEPTEMBER 2026, against June 2026 as recently as 2026-09-23), and the Mumbai retail prints are strong and deep: TMT 10 mm Rs 65,750/t (1m +15.5%, 3m +13.5%, 1y +21.0%, high_since 2026-04-30), HR coil 2.50 mm Rs 76,900/t (1m +10.8%, 3m +12.8%, 1y +29.2%, high_since 2022-05-31) and CR coil 0.63 mm Rs 89,670/t (1m +14.0%, 3m +14.9%, 1y +31.6%, high_since 2022-05-31). All three carry stats.deep true (n = 49-51 readings), so the high_since verdicts are allowed to be quoted: the Mumbai HRC and CR prints are at their highest since MAY 2022 on this series - a 4.5-year high, NOT an all-time high, measured over 50 monthly readings. Two caveats stated rather than buried: the series is stamped 30-Sep-2026, i.e. about two months lagged, so '1m' is August-to-September; and no basis_break applies to it. WHY NO CARD: the group's only mapped small-cap beneficiary is Vraj Iron and Steel (mcap Rs 406.8 cr), which is ALREADY PUBLISHED; the other mapped benefit names (Tata Steel, JSW, SAIL, Jindal Steel) are far above the Rs 25,000 cr ceiling at which the three-year study found no 5x at all, and the two names in the band on the SUFFER side (APL Apollo, Hariom Pipe - converters) cannot be published because this page writes no short ideas. Carried as a watch, and as the open task of adding a second documented small-cap long-products or HRC producer to commodity_map.json once one can be verified from its own product-mix disclosure.

researched.name: Freshara Agro Exports Ltd
researched.reason: The one name today with a hard, document-verified trigger in the right size band. India order book Rs 170 cr (deck: Rs 160 cr) against Rs 91 cr a year earlier, +86.8%, both ends read from the company's own call transcripts in this run. The number that makes it an idea is the differential, not the headline: India STANDALONE revenue grew only 22.4% in the same half (Rs ~140 cr to Rs 171.42 cr, deck), so the running book is moving about three times faster than the business it belongs to, and the company explains why - 'both the newly installed production lines are already fully booked with new customer orders. For the first time in years, we are outnumbered by customers' orders than the lines present with us'. H1 FY27 consolidated total income Rs 260.01 cr (+84.54%), EBITDA Rs 34.58 cr (+41.84%), PAT Rs 20.97 cr (+40.61%), EPS Rs 8.92; the acquired Spanish olive business (Aceitunas Sarasa) contributed Rs 95.29 cr at a 12.3% EBITDA margin in its first consolidated half. Market cap Rs 916 cr at Rs 389.85, 21.6x trailing and 19.5x forward on guidance of Rs 575-600 cr with margins merely stable. Published at MEDIUM confidence with eleven red flags written in, the three that matter being: the statutory H1 FY27 results PDF is IMAGE-ONLY (14 pages, 1,779 extractable characters) so the balance sheet, debt, related-party and auditor pages were not read; standalone inventory ~Rs 120 cr and trade receivables ~Rs 120-121 cr, about four months of sales, which the CMD attributes to Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz transit delays; and an undecided Rs 50-100 cr funding need management puts at '50-50' between debt and an equity raise. Also flagged: the deck and the same day's transcript give two different order books (160 vs 170) and the deck footnotes the figure as a management estimate; and the line barely trades - 8,100 shares on 27-Nov.

note:
A thin day in two lanes and a clean one in the third. The government lane kept nothing out of 38 PIB releases, which is the correct answer; the commodity lane's ranking is still being driven by a seven-month-stale WPI panel and its one genuinely fresh signal has no publishable small cap behind it; and the filings lane produced one new name whose order was too small to matter. The work that paid was the order-book ledger.

**What was published.** One card: Freshara Agro Exports (NSE Emerge, mcap Rs 916 cr), on a confirmed order-book jump. The jump itself is only half the reason. Rs 170 cr against Rs 91 cr a year earlier is +86.8%, but the company's own definition of that book - 'a running order book ... for three months to six months' against which it ships Rs 30+ cr a month - means the level is half a year of visibility, not a backlog, and the deck footnotes it as a management estimate. What makes it an idea is the DIFFERENTIAL: India standalone revenue grew 22.4% in the same half while the India order book grew 86.8%. The consolidated +84.5% headline is the Spanish acquisition and would have misled anyone who stopped there; the deck shows both, to the company's credit, and this card uses the India numbers throughout.

**Two filings that said the opposite of what they appeared to say.** Sahaj Solar's press release was reported on X by CNBC-TV18 as the company having 'bagged a Rs 389.52 crore order from Mauritius'; the release says it received a Letter of Intent for two projects it will OWN through its own Mauritius subsidiaries, with CEB as the power offtaker and the USD 42 mn described as a 'preliminary' estimated project value. The stock rose 15.3% on 91,600 shares against a normal 5,000-11,000. Our own screen made the same mistake in the other direction - it converted the USD 42 mn to Rs 388.23 cr and set it against the Rs 300 cr order book as an order win, giving a 1.294x flag. Both are now recorded as NOT A FLAG with the quotes. And Oriana Power's filing arrived under NSE's heading 'Change in Auditors', which reads as a red flag; it is a routine re-appointment of the same SECRETARIAL auditor, and the substantive item in the same filing is board approval to migrate from NSE Emerge to the Main Board and list on BSE. A reader who trusted either headline would have been wrong twice.

**The best price fact of the day is one we cannot trade.** A new Ministry of Steel monthly report landed, taking the committed Mumbai series from June to September 2026, and Mumbai HR coil (Rs 76,900/t) and CR coil (Rs 89,670/t) are at their highest since MAY 2022 on a 50-reading monthly series, with TMT up 15.5% in a month. It is deep enough to quote a high_since verdict and it is a domestic rupee print rather than a Shanghai proxy. It produced no card because the steel group's only mapped small-cap beneficiary, Vraj Iron and Steel, is already published, and everything else mapped is either above the Rs 25,000 cr ceiling at which no 5x occurred in three years or sits on the suffer side as a converter. Finding a second documented small-cap long-products or HRC producer for commodity_map.json is the open task this leaves.

**The updates sweep was the bulk of the run.** 42 new non-routine filings across 19 cards; 13 updates written. Nine of the 42 were filings yesterday's run had already written up - the queue flags anything filed on or after updates_checked as new, which includes the previous run's own work - and no duplicate was written. The ones a holder would actually want to know: Susan Electricals' promoter subscribing Rs 19.39 cr of warrants at Rs 262 when the stock trades at Rs 212.80, which is 23% ABOVE market and the inverse of the usual preferential-issue red flag; Oriana's Main Board migration; Viviana at L1 on Rs 463.57 cr, about half of a full year's guided revenue, with the L1-not-an-award caveat stated as loudly as the number; NSE refusing Highway Infrastructure's valuation report as first filed; a Shining Tools compliance officer resigning with immediate effect and no successor; and promoter or promoter-group buying at three separate cards (GP Eco, Prime Cable, Sugs Lloyd), small in rupees but broad in participation.

**What this run could not do.** www.dgtr.gov.in has now been blocked for two consecutive days, and the trade-remedy docket is where the PLAYBOOK's own TRADE rule lives - written after OCCL rose 43% while the scan showed it only as a volume spike. Two live anti-dumping investigations sit unread: toluene di-isocyanate from China, Japan and Korea, and clavulanic acid from China and the EU. Neither notice could be opened, so the petitioning domestic industry - the whole point - is unknown. Separately, both X post bodies and ValuePickr threads were unreadable, so two of the three required sweeps ran on search snippets alone; that is stated inside each published section rather than hidden here, and 'nothing on X' is nowhere claimed.

It is neither an order (the release says Letter of Intent, PPA 'to be executed on award') nor revenue to the company (the projects are '100% owned by Sahaj Solar ... through a wholly owned subsidiary'). Recorded NOT A FLAG with the quotes. The underlying gap is that the letter-reader has no test for 'project the company will own' versus 'order the company received'.
